newsitem.title: CANADA: Morrison disputes Canadian 88 CEO comments.
newsitem.headline: Morrison disputes Canadian 88 CEO comments.

text.p: Morrison Petroleums Ltd on Thursday strongly disputed accusations by the chief executive of Canadian 88 Energy Corp that Morrison was under reporting its development costs and misleading shareholders.
"We don't appreciate him making misrepresentations about our information in what we consider to be a fairly sensitive time," Morrison vice-president Paul Charron said.

Greg Noval, chief executive of Canadian 88, which has launched a hostile takeover for Morrison, told Reuters that Canadian 88's analysis showed Morrison's finding and development costs were several dollars per barrel higher than reported Wednesday in Morrison's 1996 year-end data.
He also said Morrison may not have been "leveling with their shareholders."

Morrison is the target of a C$652 million hostile takeover bid from Canadian 88. At stake are potentially rich natural gas reserves in the foothills of southern Alberta, where Morrison is a large acreage holder.
"Let's be clear -- we have calculated our finding and development costs on precisely the same basis that we have calculated them on for the past five years," Charron said.
"And those finding and development costs are reviewed by our auditors on an annual basis. The methodology is precisely the same."
Morrison reported its finding and development costs were C$2.13 per barrel of oil equivalent for proven plus probable reserves in 1996, a big improvement over the showing in 1995.
The calculation, which shows how much an oil company spends exploring and drilling for oil and gas and bringing it on stream, is a measure of how efficient a firm is in operating.
Noval has said one of the reason's for Morrison's recent history of disappointing stock performance has been its high costs.
"I'm not sure what his motive is, but our motive is to provide our shareholders with information on the results of the company," Charron said.
The company is expected to make a recommendation to shareholders on the Canadian 88 offer on Monday.
